rule: fidelity per rule status (contract.mjs); SOURCE_EXACT only on HARD / HIGH / original-checked #709 rules; every derivation written down

derivations.derivation: the Turtles received weekly N / unit sheets (CONTEXTUAL operational practice); the same formula is evaluated on every session with the value of the prior close, which uses no later information
equities: dollars per point = 1 per share, so a unit is floor(0.01 x notional / N) whole shares; N is the value at the prior close (no same-day information)

Dennis set the yearly notional account subjectively; the adaptation uses actual equity at the first session of each year (as PR #779 / #705); cuts compound per the printed example (1.0 -> 0.8 -> 0.64)
long-only adaptation: only the 12-unit long limit can bind
daily bars: the buy stop fills at max(open, trigger) on the bar whose high reaches the trigger (the rule itself); one tick = 0.01 raw price converted to the split-adjusted basis

skip only after a profitable last breakout (TUR-S1SKIP); a 10-day exit at a loss without a prior 2N adverse move is neither a loser (TUR-S1LOSER) nor profitable, so the next signal is taken (the #705 engine skipped it); how a still open breakout counts is the separate SOURCE_AMBIGUOUS rule TUR-SF-S1-OPEN-BREAKOUT; daily-bar path: the level nearer to the open is reached first (model assumption MA-TUR-HELD-BAR-ORDER); the filter is warmed on the history before the window

N for add spacing and stops is N of the initial entry (the printed examples keep N constant); the next level is 1/2 N above the last actual fill even if that unit was stopped out since; after a unit stop-out the position takes no further adds (a re-add would be the optional Whipsaw re-entry, not implemented); the first add of a bar fills at max(open, level), later adds of the same bar at their level
consequence of TUR-ADD on daily bars; no extra rule
not a separate rule: the consequence of TUR-STOPADD that the worked example TUR-CRUDE prints (27.70, 27.70, 27.70, 28.40); reproduced by a golden case

the opposite channel breakout uses the same one-tick convention as the entry (0.01 raw, split-adjusted); fill min(open, level) on daily bars (review SF-R1-06); on the entry bar the level is a resting stop like the unit stops: a low through it is assumed after the entry, the higher of unit stop and channel level is reached first (sf-turtle-1.1.0)

TUR-RANKVAR (OPTIONAL) allows several normalisations; the one the source names, (close - close 3 months ago) / N with 3 months = 63 sessions at the prior close, is used; ties by security id. Without group data all simultaneous signals form one group.

DAR-Q11 (CONTEXTUAL) describes selling on the stop after a lower box break; for a box without position the box simply no longer exists. State transition, not a selection filter.

"a fraction" is not quantified: VU convention = one raw cent converted to the split-adjusted basis (the smallest price increment); fill = max(open, trigger) on daily bars; the reviewer may set a different fraction (DAR-C-THIO)
same one-cent fraction as DAR-SF-ENTRY; on the entry bar a low at or below the stop exits (pessimistic daily-bar order)

weekly bar = ISO week of the daily snapshot bars (open of the first, high/low of the week, close of the last session, summed volume); a week is complete only after its last session; simple 30-week mean of weekly closes

"below or at a falling MA": reject when the buy price (the buy-stop trigger, prepared from the completed prior week) is at or below MA30w, or MA30w is below its value one week earlier; the prior close vs the MA is reported as evidence (a Stage 1 -> 2 breakout crosses both in the same week, review SF-R1-02); one-week comparison is the smallest observable slope (no threshold added)
the candidate record carries the buy-stop level (resistance + one raw cent); WEIN-LIM stop-limit spacing is an execution example (EXAMPLE_ONLY), not modelled
every candidate record carries a proposed stop before any decision; the reviewer confirms or replaces it

resistance = highest weekly high from the week the MA30w last stopped falling (start of the base) to the prior week; no minimum base length (WEIN-BASE: no fixed ten weeks).
